Williams-Goss''' (born September 16, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] of the [[Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]], with the 55th overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. He spent two seasons with the [[University of Washington]]'s [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Huskies]], before deciding to transfer before the 2015–16 season. At a height of {{convert|6|ft|3|in|m|abbr=on}} tall, he plays at the [[point guard]] position. ==High school career== [[File:20130403 MCDAAG Nigel Williams-Goss at the rim.JPG|Williams-Goss at the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]|thumb|upright|left]] Nigel Williams-Goss played high school basketball at [[Findlay Prep]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]] and was the program's first 4-year player and helped lead the team to a 124–8 record, including winning the High School National Championship in 2010 and 2012.{{cite web|title=Findlay Prep's Nigel Williams-Goss named to McDonald's All-American team|url=http://lasvegassun.com/news/2013/feb/14/findlay-preps-nigel-williams-goss-named-mcdonalds-/|date=February 14, 2013}} He maintained a 4.0 GPA throughout his time in high school, while attending classes at Henderson International School.{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss' Strong Faith Paves Way To Success|url=http://archive.usab.com/mens/u19/13_mu19_features_williams-goss.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150915005625/http://archive.usab.com/mens/u19/13_mu19_features_williams-goss.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 15, 2015|date=June 17, 2013}} MaxPreps named Williams-Goss an honorable mention sophomore All-American in 2011.{{cite web|title=Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/_YxfCGxkEeCkhgAcxJSkrA/boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm|date=April 21, 2011}} After helping lead Findlay Prep to a High School National Championship, while averaging 15 points, 4.9 assists, and 4 rebounds per game, he was named a third-team junior All-American by MaxPreps in 2012.{{cite web|title=Boys Basketball Junior All-American Team|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/article.aspx?articleid=d1d546fd-5d58-4414-8321-71305642ae0b&page=3|date=April 16, 2012}} As a senior, Williams-Goss averaged more than 18 points and 7 assists per game and was named to MaxPreps' first-team All-American team, after leading Findlay Prep 54 consecutive wins, including a 35–1 record and a trip to the semifinals of the National High School Invitational in the 2012–13 season.{{cite web|title=MaxPreps 2013 Boys Basketball All-American Team|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/bqRarSiJFkCjG8PM2lhOZA/maxpreps-2013-boys-basketball-all-american-team.htm|date=April 11, 2013}} He was also named to [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|Parade Magazine's All-America team]]{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss makes Parade All-America team|url=http://blogs.seattletimes.com/huskymensbasketball/2013/05/22/nigel-williams-goss-makes-parada-all-america-team/|date=May 22, 2013}} Williams-Goss was named as to the prestigious [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2013 McDonald's All-American Game]] Against the best high school seniors in the nation, he scored 10 points along with 6 assists, 2 rebounds, 2 blocks, and a steal, while shooting 4-for-6 from the field and 2-for-2 from the free throw line. He also won the 3-point contest during the McDonald's All-American game festivities.{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss shines at McDonald's All-American game|url=http://blogs.seattletimes.com/huskymensbasketball/2013/04/03/nigel-williams-goss-shines-at-mcdonalds-all-american-game/|date=April 3, 2013}} Williams-Goss was also invited to the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], where he led the West team to a 102–98 victory over the East, delivering the game-winning basket, in which he stole the ball and converted a three-point play after sinking a layup and heading to the foul line for an additional point. He finished with 17 points, 4 assists, 3 rebounds, and 1 steal on 5-for-6 from 2-point range, 1–1 from beyond the 3-point arc, and 4-of-5 from the free throw line in 20 minutes of play.{{cite web|title=California Supreme Alumni Nigel Williams-Goss Shines in 2013 Jordan Classic Making the Game Winning Shot, and Leading the West Roster with 17 Points|url=https://californiasupremebasketball.com/2013/04/14/california-supreme-alumni-nigel-williams-goss-shines-in-2013-jordan-classic-making-the-game-winning-shot-and-leading-the-west-roster-with-17-points/|date=April 14, 2013|access-date=April 23, 2016|archive-date=May 8, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160508175239/https://californiasupremebasketball.com/2013/04/14/california-supreme-alumni-nigel-williams-goss-shines-in-2013-jordan-classic-making-the-game-winning-shot-and-leading-the-west-roster-with-17-points/|url-status=dead}} ===Recruiting=== {{quote box|width=23em|align=right|quote="He is a great floor general. He is very intelligent and has high, high basketball I.Q. He understands what it takes to win and is a great leader. Guys like him don't come around very often."|source=— [[Lorenzo Romar]], Washington Head Coach.{{cite web|title=Romar Signs Another Guard To Next Year's Class |url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=749597&SPID=126628&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=30200&ATCLID=208025529 |date=November 16, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160514043914/http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=749597&SPID=126628&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=30200&ATCLID=208025529 |archive-date=May 14, 2016 }}}} In December 2010, after beginning his sophomore year at Findlay Prep, Williams-Goss announced his commitment to UNLV. At the time he was being heavily pursued by the Rebels, along with Arizona, Washington, Oregon, and Oregon State, with increased interest from Georgetown and Connecticut.{{cite web|title=Findlay Prep sophomore guard Nigel Williams-Goss verbally commits to UNLV|url=http://lasvegassun.com/news/2010/dec/15/williamsgoss-commit-121510/|date=December 15, 2010}} In April 2011, [[Lon Kruger]] jumped ship from the head coaching job at UNLV to become the new head coach at Oklahoma. Two weeks later, Williams-Goss decommitted from UNLV, giving other programs, including the Rebels' coaching staff a chance to court him.{{cite web|title=Findlay Prep sophomore Nigel Williams-Goss officially de-commits from UNLV|url=http://lasvegassun.com/news/2011/apr/17/findlay-prep-sophomore-nigel-williams-goss-officia/|date=April 17, 2011}} Even though he re-opened his recruitment, overall = #33 | 247 overall = #33 | espn overall = #19 | accessdate = April 15, 2016 | bball = yes }} ==College career== ===Freshman year=== As a freshman, Williams-Goss started every game, while averaging 13.4 points, 4.4 assists, 4.4 rebounds, and 1.1 steals. His stellar season earned him a selection to the All-[[2013–14 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12]] Freshman Team.{{cite web|title=2013–14 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2014/3/10/2013-14-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|date=March 10, 2014}} He led the Pac-12 conference freshmen in scoring, assists, and assist-to-turnover ratio (1.6). He set a new UW freshman single-season record with 140 assists. Despite his phenomenal year, UW finished with a disappointing 17–15 record (9–9 in Pac-12 games), losing in the first round of the Pac-12 Tournament to Utah, and missed the postseason for the first time since 2007, after declining an invitation to the CBI.{{cite web|title=Washington Basketball Profile: Nigel Williams-Goss|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208952660|access-date=April 16, 2015}} In his first collegiate game, he posted 6 points, 6 assists, 3 rebounds, 3 steals, and a season-best 1 block on 2-for-7 field goal shooting and 2-for-2 from the free throw line in an 88–78 win over inner-city rival Seattle University.{{cite web|title=Official Basketball Box Score – Seattle University vs Washington |url=http://www.gohuskies.com/pdf9/2562912.pdf |date=November 10, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160601163328/http://www.gohuskies.com/pdf9/2562912.pdf |archive-date=June 1, 2016 }} On November 17, he had 22 points, 6 rebounds, 5 assists, and a season-high 3 steals on 9-for-15 from the field and 4-for-5 from the charity stripe in a 92–80 win over Eastern Washington.{{cite web|title=Nigel-Williams BOSS: Freshman Leads UW Rally Over EWU|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209311234&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=November 17, 2013}} On November 26, he scored 20 points, along with 6 assists and 3 assists on 5-of-8 2-point shooting, 1-of-1 from 3-point, and 7-of-8 free throws in an 83–79 win over Montana.{{cite web|title=3-J Wilcox Rescues Huskies In 83–79 Rally Past Montana|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209324972&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=November 26, 2013}} On January 18, 2014, Williams-Goss posted 17 points, 7 rebounds, 6 assists, and 1 steal on 3-for-7 2-pointers, 3-for-5 from 3-point land, and 2-for-3 free throws in a 79–67 loss to Stanford.{{cite web|title=Stanford Hands Washington 79–67 Loss|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209378756&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=January 18, 2014}} On January 25, he set a new UW freshman single-game scoring record with 32 points in come-from-behind 87–81 win over Oregon State, in which he shot 7-for-11 from 2-point range, a season-best 3-for-4 from beyond the 3-point line, 9-for-10 from the free throw line, along with 5 rebounds, 3 assists, 1 steal, and zero turnovers.{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-BOSS: Freshman's Record 32 Points Beat Oregon St. 87–81|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209386033&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=January 25, 2014}} On February 22, Williams-Goss dished out a season-high 10 assists to go along with 14 points, 2 rebounds, and 1 steal on 7-for-10 field goal shooting in an 86–62 win over Oregon State.{{cite web|title=Wilcox, Williams-Goss Lead UW Uprising At Oregon St In 86–62 Win|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209414682&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=February 22, 2014}} On February 28, he grabbed a season-high 12 rebounds, along with 17 points, 4 assists, and 2 steals on 6-of-10 2-point field goals, 1-of-2 3-pointers, and 2-of-3 free throws om 30 minutes, in a 72–49 win over cross-state rival Washington State.{{cite web|title=Williams-Goss, Andrews Lead Huskies' 72–49 Roll Over WSU|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209420741&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=February 28, 2014}} ===Sophomore year=== As a sophomore, he led the [[2014–15 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|2014–15 Huskies]] in points (15.6 scoring average) and assists (5.9 per game). He also contributed 4.7 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game, while starting in 30 of the team's 31 games. His standout sophomore season earned him second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] in the [[2014–15 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12]].{{cite web|title=2014–15 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2015/3/9/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|date=March 9, 2015}} He was also named as a third-team [[Academic All-American]], while boasting a 3.74 cumulative GPA in pre-social science.{{cite web|title=NWG Named Capitol One Third Team Academic All-American |url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30200&ATCLID=209909801 |date=February 26, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160601163330/http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30200&ATCLID=209909801 |archive-date=June 1, 2016 }} Washington began the year with an 11–0 record, including impressive wins over Oklahoma and San Diego State, matching the best start in Lorenzo Romar's tenure as the Huskies' coach. Despite such a promising start, Washington would lose 15 of its last 20 games, finishing with a 16–15 record (5–13 in Pac-12 games), losing in the first round of the Pac-12 Tournament to Stanford, and missed the postseason yet again, after declining an invitation to the CBI. In his first game as a sophomore at Washington on November 14, 2014, Williams-Goss grabbed a career-high 12 rebounds, along with 10 points, 7 assists, 2 steals, and 1 block on 5-of-5 2-point shooting in a 77–59 win over South Carolina State.{{cite web|title=Huskies Cruise Past SC State, 77–59|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209766842&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=November 14, 2014}} On November 28, he dished out a career-high 12 assists to go along with 21 points and 7 rebounds on 6-for-14 field goals and 5-for-6 free throws in an 80–70 win over Long Beach State.{{cite web|title=Williams-Goss' Double Double Lifts UW Past Long Beach State, 80–70|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209786152&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=November 28, 2014}} On January 2, 2015, in an 81–75 loss to Cal, Williams-Goss came the closest to a triple-double in his college career, posting 19 points, 9 assists, and 8 rebounds on 7-for-16 from the field and 5-for-6 from the free throw line.{{cite web|title=No. 21 Men's Basketball Drops Pac-12 Opener to California, 81–75|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209832802&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=January 2, 2015}} In an 80–77 loss to Washington State on January 10, Williams-Goss dropped 30 points, 7 rebounds, 5 assists, and career-highs of 3 steals and 1 block on 13-for-22 field goals and 4-of-4 from the charity stripe.{{cite web|title=Dawgs Fall to Washington State, 80–77|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209843909&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=January 10, 2015}} In a loss to Cal on February 1, he posted a season-high 31 points along with 6 rebounds, 5 assists, 1 steal, and zero turnovers on 8-of-11 2-pointers, 3-for-6 3-point field goals, and 6-of-6 free throws.{{cite web|title=Dawgs Suffer 90–88 Loss to California|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209871859&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=February 1, 2015}} On February 15, he had 20 points, 6 assists, and 5 rebounds on 6-of-15 within the arc, 1-of-3 beyond the 3-point arc, field goals and 5-of-5 free throws in a loss to Arizona State.{{cite web|title=Washington comes up short, falls to Arizona State 78–68|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209892625&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=February 15, 2015}} In a win over Washington State on February 22, he had 20 points, 7 assists, 3 rebounds, and 2 steals on 6-of-10 2-pointers, 1-for-3 from 3-point land, and 5-of-8 free throws.{{cite web|title=Andrew Andrews' Late Three Lifts Huskies Over Cougars|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209902607&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=February 22, 2015}} In the regular season finale against Utah on March 7, Williams-Goss posted 28 points, 6 rebounds, 3 assists, and 2 steals on 10-for-16 2-point field goals, 1-of-2 3-pointers, and 5-for-7 free throws in a 77–68 win over #13 Utah.{{cite web|title=Huskies Upset No. 13 Utah, 77–68, on Senior Day in Seattle|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209933700&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=March 7, 2015}} ===Junior year=== {{quote box|width=23em|align=right|quote="Nigel is a proven high-level player who possesses all of the qualities that we admire here at Gonzaga. He's a very driven, team-oriented guy and is excited to be a part of this program. He's also been great in the classroom as an Academic All-American, which fits in with our history of academic success. We are really excited to get him in here and help him develop the next part of his game."|source=— [[Mark Few]], Gonzaga Head Coach.{{cite web|title=Gonzaga Men's Basketball Adds UW Transfer Nigel Williams-Goss|url=http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/050615aaa.html|date=May 6, 2015|access-date=April 20, 2016|archive-date=April 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428091916/http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/050615aaa.html|url-status=dead}}}} In April 2015, Williams-Goss announced he was leaving Washington and transferring to another school. Even though he had a great relationship with Coach Romar and his teammates, he was uncomfortable with the changes surrounding the program and the team's consistent losing.{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss explains why he's leaving Washington|url=http://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/nigel-williams-goss-explains-why-hes-leaving-washington/|date=April 10, 2015}} He initially claimed he was considering UNLV, Texas, Georgetown, Michigan State, Arkansas, and Gonzaga.{{cite web|title=Washington transfer Nigel Williams-Goss told @CBSSports he is considering UNLV, Texas, Georgetown, Michigan State, Arkansas, and Gonzaga|url=https://twitter.com/JonRothstein/status/586628584040706048|date=April 10, 2015}} A couple days later, he said he would take visits to UNLV, Providence, Texas, and Georgetown, with Michigan State also in the mix.{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss told @CBSSports he will visit UNLV this wknd, Providence (4/25), Texas (5/1), + Georgetown (5/8). Mich St also in mix |url=https://twitter.com/JonRothstein/status/588024600769990656|date=April 14, 2015}} After visiting UNLV and Providence, Williams-Goss cut his list to 4 (UNLV, Providence, Gonzaga, and Ohio State), with plans to visit Gonzaga and Ohio State.{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss told @CBSSports he will visit Ohio State on 5/8. Visits Gonzaga this weekend. Also considering PC + UNLV. List cut to 4 |url=https://twitter.com/JonRothstein/status/592858097317781504|date=April 27, 2015}} He called off his trip to Ohio State after committing to Gonzaga during his recruiting trip. He would have to redshirt the 2015–16 season before having two years of eligibility to play at the beginning of the 2016–17 season.{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss will transfer to Gonzaga|url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2015/may/03/nigel-williams-goss-will-transfer-gonzaga/|date=May 3, 2015}} Williams-Goss cited the Zags' track record of developing players during their redshirt year, winning at a high level, and their up-tempo offense which includes a ton of ball screens for his commitment to Gonzaga.{{cite web|title=Gonzaga Basketball: Introducing our newest Zag, repping #5 Nigel Williams-Goss! Welcome to the squad Nigel!|url=https://twitter.com/ZagMBB/status/596069451914715138|date=May 6, 2015}} Throughout his junior season, Williams-Goss provided his best season in college with his only season in Gonzaga. In 38 games he played with for Gonzaga, he recorded the most points off of his best overall shooting percentage, rebounds, and steals per game while also playing the fewest minutes per game throughout his college career. In addition to those results, he was also named the [[West Coast Conference]]'s Newcomer of The Year and the [[West Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|West Coast Conference's Player of The Year]], as well as became a member of the All-West Coast Conference First Team, a member of the [[Academic All-American]] First Team, and was a consensus All-American Second Team for the help he provided for the 37–2 Gonzaga Bulldogs. Not only that, but he also helped lead Gonzaga to its first ever NCAA Championship match, where they ultimately lost to the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]]. After the end of the NCAA Tournament, Williams-Goss was one of a record-high 182 underclassmen to declare for the [[2017 NBA draft]], with him signing up with an agent on the day of his declaration. ==Professional career== ===Partizan Belgrade (2017–2018)=== On June 23, 2017, Williams-Goss was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] as the 55th pick of the [[2017 NBA draft]]. After playing for the Jazz in the [[2017 NBA Summer League]], he signed a two-year contract with Serbian club [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] on August 28, 2017.{{cite news|title=Najdžel Vilijams-Gos dve godine u Partizanu|url=http://kkpartizan.rs/sr/vest/2104/najdzel-vilijams-gos-dve-godine-u-partizanu|access-date=August 28, 2017|work=kkpartizan.rs|date=August 28, 2017|language=sr}} On February 18, 2018, Williams-Goss recorded 23 points, along with 7 assists, 3 rebounds and 2 steals, and led Partizan to win the Serbian [[2017–18 Radivoj Korać Cup|2018 Radivoj Korać Cup]], after an 81–75 win over [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]]. He was subsequently named [[Radivoj Korać Cup MVP Award|the Serbian Cup MVP]].{{cite news|title=Partizan NIS winner of the Triglav Insurance Radivoj Korac Cup 2018!|url=http://kss.rs/eng/partizan-nis-winner-of-the-triglav-insurance-radivoj-korac-cup-2018/|access-date=July 5, 2018|work=kss.rs|date=February 18, 2018|archive-date=August 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180805154609/http://kss.rs/eng/partizan-nis-winner-of-the-triglav-insurance-radivoj-korac-cup-2018/|url-status=dead}} In 46 games played during the 2017–18 season (played in the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]], [[ABA League]], [[Serbian Basketball League|Serbian League]], and [[Serbian Basketball Cup|Serbian Cup]] competitions), Williams-Goss averaged 17.3 points, 7 assists, 3.4 rebounds and 1.2 steals per game. ===Olympiacos (2018–2019)=== On July 5, 2018, Williams-Goss signed a three-year deal with Greek team [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], of the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite news|title=Olympiacos pens Williams-Goss to multiyear deal|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/europe/greece/280329/olympiacos-signs-nigel-williams-goss.html|access-date=July 5, 2018|work=EuroLeague.net|date=July 5, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=November 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} On July 15, 2019, Olympiacos announced that Williams-Goss had exercised his one million dollar buy-out option in order to join the [[Utah Jazz]]. ===Utah Jazz (2019–2020)=== On July 19, 2019, Williams-Goss signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|title=Jazz Sign Nigel Williams-Goss|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-sign-nigel-william-goss|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 19, 2019|date=July 19, 2019}} ===Lokomotiv Kuban (2021)=== On January 5, 2021, Russian club [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]] announced that they had signed Williams-Goss.{{cite web|title=Loko signed Nigel Williams-Goss|url=https://lokobasket.com/en/news/138310|date=January 5, 2021|website=lokobasket.com|access-date=January 5, 2021}} ===Real Madrid (2021–2023)=== On June 16, 2021, Williams-Goss signed a two-year contract with Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and [[EuroLeague]] powerhouse [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]]. During the 2021–2022 campaign, in 29 EuroLeague games (16 starts), he averaged 5.8 points, 2.1 rebounds and 2.4 assists, playing around 17 minutes per contest. During the 2022–2023 campaign, in 26 EuroLeague games (23 starts), he averaged 7.4 points, 1.3 rebounds and 1.8 assists, playing around 16 minutes per contest. In the latter season, Williams-Goss became a [[2022-23 EuroLeague|EuroLeague champion]] with the historic club. He also won the [[2021–22 ACB season|2022 Liga ACB]] championship title, as well as two domestic Supercups. On June 27, 2023, he parted ways with the team. ===Return to Olympiacos (2023–2025)=== On June 28, 2023, Williams-Goss made his return to Olympiacos after four seasons, signing a two-year contract. On June 10, 2025, he announced his departure from the club. ===Žalgiris Kaunas (2025–present)=== On June 25, 2025, Williams-Goss signed a two–year (2+1) contract with [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|url=https://zalgiris.lt/en/naujienos/zalgiris-strengthens-the-lineup-with-the-euroleague-champion#article|title=Zalgiris strengthens the lineup with the EuroLeague champion|last=|first=|date=June 25, 2025|website=zalgiris.lt|language=En|access-date=June 25, 2025}} On 25 October 2025, he suffered a hamstring muscle injury resulting in him missing several matches. ==National team career==
